translations.idiomatic: Zhili from youth to white hair annually read the Five Classics, stopping after one cycle.

sentences.zh: 每開卷，必正衣冠危坐，未嘗少懈焉。

translations.literal: Each time opening a book he always straightened cap and robe and sat upright, never slackening slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Each time opening a book he always straightened cap and robe and sat upright, never slackening slightly.

sentences.zh: 咸平初卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xianping he died, aged seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 子從吉。

translations.literal: His son Congji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Congji.

translations.literal: 〈Son〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Son〉

sentences.zh: 從吉

translations.literal: Congji
translations.idiomatic: Congji

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，改授衛尉卿，糾察在京刑獄，拜右諫議大夫，判吏部銓。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, investigating capital criminal cases; appointed Right Remonstrance Councillor; administrator of the Ministry of Personnel Selection.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu changed to Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, investigating capital criminal cases. Appointed Right Remonstrance Councillor. Administrator of the Ministry of Personnel Selection.

sentences.zh: 初，選人試判多藉地而坐，從吉以公錢市莞席給之。

translations.literal: Earlier candidates for document judgment mostly sat on the ground; Congji used public funds to buy rush mats and provide them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier candidates for document judgment mostly sat on the ground. Congji used public funds to buy rush mats and provide them.

sentences.zh: 臨事敏速，勤心公家，所至務察，多請對陳事，上謂其無隱。

translations.literal: Handling affairs swiftly and diligently devoted to public affairs; wherever he went he strove to inspect; often requested audience to state affairs; the emperor said he hid nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Handling affairs swiftly and diligently devoted to public affairs. Wherever he went he strove to inspect. Often requested audience to state affairs. The emperor said he hid nothing.

sentences.zh: 八年，改給事中、權知開封府。

translations.literal: In the eighth year changed to supervising censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year changed to supervising censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 既受命，召戒之曰：“京府浩穰，凡事太速則誤，太緩則滯，惟須酌中耳。

translations.literal: Upon receiving appointment summoned and admonished: "The capital prefecture is vast and crowded; in all affairs too fast errs, too slow stalls—only the mean is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Upon receiving appointment summoned and admonished, "The capital prefecture is vast and crowded. In all affairs too fast errs, too slow stalls—only the mean is needed.

sentences.zh: 請屬一無所受。

translations.literal: Requests and entreaties—accept none."
translations.idiomatic: Requests and entreaties—accept none."

sentences.zh: ”才數月，有咸平縣民張斌妻盧氏，訴侄質被酒詬悖。

translations.literal: Only several months later there was Xianping County commoner Zhang Bin whose wife Lady Lu sued nephew Zhi for drunken abuse and insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Only several months later there was Xianping County commoner Zhang Bin whose wife Lady Lu sued nephew Zhi for drunken abuse and insolence.

sentences.zh: 張素豪族，質本養子，而證左明白，質賄於吏。

translations.literal: The Zhangs were originally a powerful clan; Zhi was originally an adopted son yet evidence was clear; Zhi bribed officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhangs were originally a powerful clan. Zhi was originally an adopted son yet evidence was clear. Zhi bribed officials.

sentences.zh: 從吉子大理寺丞銳時督運石塘河，往來咸平，為請於縣宰，斷復質劉姓，第令與盧同居。

translations.literal: Congji's son Court of Judicial Review secretary Rui then supervised transport of the Shitang River; coming and going through Xianping he requested of the county magistrate; judgment restored Zhi to the Liu surname, only ordering cohabitation with Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Congji's son Court of Judicial Review secretary Rui then supervised transport of the Shitang River. Coming and going through Xianping he requested of the county magistrate. Judgment restored Zhi to the Liu surname, only ordering cohabitation with Lu.

sentences.zh: 質洎盧迭為訟，縣聞於府。

translations.literal: Zhi and Lu repeatedly sued each other; the county reported to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Lu repeatedly sued each other. The county reported to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 從吉命戶曹參軍呂楷就縣推問。

translations.literal: Congji ordered Household Affairs Administrator Lü Kai to go to the county to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Congji ordered Household Affairs Administrator Lü Kai to go to the county to investigate.

sentences.zh: 盧之從叔虢略尉昭一賂白金三百兩於楷，楷久不決。

translations.literal: Lu's cousin Guolue Commandery Lieutenant Zhao Yi bribed Kai with three hundred taels of white gold; Kai long did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's cousin Guolue Commandery Lieutenant Zhao Yi bribed Kai with three hundred taels of white gold. Kai long did not decide.

sentences.zh: 盧兄文質又納錢七十萬於從吉長子大理寺丞鈞，鈞以其事白從吉，而隱其所受。

translations.literal: Lu's elder brother Wenzhi also paid seven hundred thousand to Congji's eldest son Court of Judicial Review secretary Jun; Jun told Congji the affair yet concealed what he received.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's elder brother Wenzhi also paid seven hundred thousand to Congji's eldest son Court of Judicial Review secretary Jun. Jun told Congji the affair yet concealed what he received.

sentences.zh: 盧又詣府列訴，即下其事右軍巡院。

translations.literal: Lu again petitioned the prefecture listing grievances; the affair was immediately handed to the Right Military Patrol Court.
translations.idiomatic: Lu again petitioned the prefecture listing grievances. The affair was immediately handed to the Right Military Patrol Court.

sentences.zh: 昭一兄澄嘗以手書達錢惟演，云寄語從吉，事逮鈞、銳，請緩之。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi's elder brother Cheng once sent a personal letter to Qian Weiyan saying relay to Congji—the affair involved Jun and Rui; please delay it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi's elder brother Cheng once sent a personal letter to Qian Weiyan saying relay to Congji—the affair involved Jun and Rui. Please delay it.

sentences.zh: 從吉頗疑懼，密請付御史臺。

translations.literal: Congji was quite suspicious and fearful; secretly requested transfer to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Congji was quite suspicious and fearful. Secretly requested transfer to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 即詔御史王奇、直史館梁固鞫之。

translations.literal: Immediately Censor Wang Qi and Historiography Compiler Liang Gu interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Immediately Censor Wang Qi and Historiography Compiler Liang Gu interrogated.

sentences.zh: 獄成，從吉坐削給事勒停，惟演罷翰林學士，楷、鈞免官，配隸衡、郢州，銳、文質皆削一官，澄、昭一並決杖配隸。

translations.literal: When the case was complete Congji was punished by stripping supervising censor and suspension; Weiyan removed as Hanlin academician; Kai and Jun dismissed from office and assigned to Heng and Ying prefectures; Rui and Wenzhi both stripped of one rank; Cheng and Zhao Yi both beaten and assigned.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was complete Congji was punished by stripping supervising censor and suspension. Weiyan removed as Hanlin academician. Kai and Jun dismissed from office and assigned to Heng and Ying prefectures. Rui and Wenzhi both stripped of one rank. Cheng and Zhao Yi both beaten and assigned.

sentences.zh: 又高清者，庫部郎中士宏之子，景德中舉進士，宰相寇準以弟之女妻之。

translations.literal: Also Gao Qing was son of Treasury Ministry director Shi Hong; during Jingde passed the jinshi; Chief Councilor Kou Zhun married him to his younger brother's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Also Gao Qing was son of Treasury Ministry director Shi Hong. During Jingde passed the jinshi. Chief Councilor Kou Zhun married him to his younger brother's daughter.

sentences.zh: 寇氏卒，故相李沆家復婿之。

translations.literal: When the Kou clan died former chief councilor Li Hang's family again married a daughter to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kou clan died former chief councilor Li Hang's family again married a daughter to him.

sentences.zh: 子官以賄聞，頗恃姻援驕縱，被服如公侯家，以是欺蠹小民。

translations.literal: Ziguan was known for bribery; quite relying on marriage connections he was arrogant and unrestrained; dress like nobles' houses; thereby deceiving and harming common people.
translations.idiomatic: Ziguan was known for bribery. Quite relying on marriage connections he was arrogant and unrestrained. Dress like nobles' houses. Thereby deceiving and harming common people.

sentences.zh: 知太康縣，民有詣府訴家產者，清納其賄，時已罷任，即逃居他所。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Taikang County; when people petitioned the prefecture about family property Qing accepted bribes; already dismissed from office he immediately fled to hide elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Taikang County. When people petitioned the prefecture about family property Qing accepted bribes. Already dismissed from office he immediately fled to hide elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 銳嘗就清貸白金七十兩，清以多納賄賂，事將敗，求以為助。

translations.literal: Rui once borrowed seventy taels of white gold from Qing; Qing because he had taken many bribes and the affair would fail sought help.
translations.idiomatic: Rui once borrowed seventy taels of white gold from Qing. Qing because he had taken many bribes and the affair would fail sought help.

sentences.zh: 時方鞫盧氏獄，從吉請對，發其事，欲以自解。

translations.literal: Just then interrogating the Lu case Congji requested audience and exposed the affair, wishing to exonerate himself.
translations.idiomatic: Just then interrogating the Lu case Congji requested audience and exposed the affair, wishing to exonerate himself.

sentences.zh: 逮清等係獄，命比部員外郎劉宗吉、御史江仲甫劾之。

translations.literal: Qing and others were imprisoned; ordered Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue Liu Zongji and Censor Jiang Zhongfu to impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Qing and others were imprisoned. Ordered Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue Liu Zongji and Censor Jiang Zhongfu to impeach.

sentences.zh: 清枉法當死，特杖脊黥面，配沙門島；

translations.literal: Qing by law deserved death; specially beaten on the back, tattooed on the face, assigned to Shamen Island;
translations.idiomatic: Qing by law deserved death. Specially beaten on the back, tattooed on the face, assigned to Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 銳又削衛尉寺丞。

translations.literal: Rui again stripped of Court of Imperial Guards secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Rui again stripped of Court of Imperial Guards secretary.

sentences.zh: 從吉坐首露在已發，當贖銅，特削諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Congji punished because disclosure came after exposure; should redeem with copper; specially stripped of Remonstrance Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Congji punished because disclosure came after exposure. Should redeem with copper. Specially stripped of Remonstrance Councillor.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，起為衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi raised to Director of the Court of Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianxi raised to Director of the Court of Imperial Guards.

sentences.zh: 明年，判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: The next year administrator of the Petition Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: The next year administrator of the Petition Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 坐與寇準親善，以光祿卿致仕。

translations.literal: Punished for closeness to Kou Zhun; retired as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for closeness to Kou Zhun. Retired as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十。

translations.literal: Before long died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long died, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 從吉喜為詩，時有警語。

translations.literal: Congji loved composing poetry and sometimes had striking phrases.
translations.idiomatic: Congji loved composing poetry and sometimes had striking phrases.

sentences.zh: 兼工醫術。

translations.literal: Also skilled in medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: Also skilled in medical arts.

sentences.zh: 子孫登仕者甚眾，第進士升朝曳朱紱者數人。

translations.literal: Descendants entering office were very numerous; several passed the jinshi and entered court wearing red.
translations.idiomatic: Descendants entering office were very numerous. Several passed the jinshi and entered court wearing red.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，尤能治生，多作負販器僦賃，以至鬻棺櫝於市。

translations.literal: The family was rich in wealth and especially good at managing livelihood; made many carrying and vending implements for rent, even selling coffins in the market.
translations.idiomatic: The family was rich in wealth and especially good at managing livelihood. Made many carrying and vending implements for rent, even selling coffins in the market.

sentences.zh: 又善為饌具，分遺權要。

translations.literal: Also skilled at preparing delicacies and distributing them to the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Also skilled at preparing delicacies and distributing them to the powerful.

sentences.zh: 晚年進趨彌篤，以至於敗，物論鄙之。

translations.literal: In later years advancement grew ever more earnest, leading to ruin; public opinion despised him.
translations.idiomatic: In later years advancement grew ever more earnest, leading to ruin. Public opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 子鏞，金部度支員外郎、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: Son Yong, vice minister of the Gold Department and Revenue and Palace Library collator.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yong, vice minister of the Gold Department and Revenue and Palace Library collator.

sentences.zh: 鍇，太常博士。

translations.literal: Kai, doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, doctor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 論曰：八政之首食貨，以國家之經費不可一日而無也。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Of the eight policies food and wealth come first, for state revenue cannot be absent even one day.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Of the eight policies food and wealth come first, for state revenue cannot be absent even one day.

sentences.zh: 然生之有道而用之有節，則存乎其人焉爾。

translations.literal: Yet if production has a way and use has measure, it depends on the man.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if production has a way and use has measure, it depends on the man.

sentences.zh: 張鑒將命西蜀，處製得宜，庶乎可與行權者也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jian received orders to western Shu and handled control appropriately—he may be counted among those who could exercise discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian received orders to western Shu and handled control appropriately—he may be counted among those who could exercise discretion.

sentences.zh: 子輿裁損經製，索湘議罷鬻茶，許驤謹守儒行，知禮篤信經學，國華不辱君命，皆有足稱者焉。

translations.literal: Ziyu trimmed institutions; Suo Xiang proposed stopping tea sales; Xu Xiang carefully maintained Confucian conduct; Zhili deeply trusted classical learning; Guohua did not disgrace the ruler's command—all had sufficient merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu trimmed institutions. Suo Xiang proposed stopping tea sales. Xu Xiang carefully maintained Confucian conduct. Zhili deeply trusted classical learning. Guohua did not disgrace the ruler's command—all had sufficient merit.

sentences.zh: 太初自謂達性命之蘊，而卒流於釋、老之歸，文寶久任邊郡，而不免以生事蒙黜，劉綜著勞朔、易而短於經術，從吉勤於公務而疏於訓子，固未得為盡善也。

translations.literal: Taichu himself claimed to comprehend the store of fate yet ultimately flowed to Buddhist and Daoist returns; Wenbao long held frontier posts yet could not avoid dismissal for stirring affairs; Liu Zong showed merit on Shuo and Yi yet was short in classical learning; Congji was diligent in public affairs yet negligent in teaching his sons—truly they did not reach complete goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Taichu himself claimed to comprehend the store of fate yet ultimately flowed to Buddhist and Daoist returns. Wenbao long held frontier posts yet could not avoid dismissal for stirring affairs. Liu Zong showed merit on Shuo and Yi yet was short in classical learning. Congji was diligent in public affairs yet negligent in teaching his sons—truly they did not reach complete goodness.

sentences.zh: 自餘諸子，之翰虧潔白之操，卞袞乏仁恕之道，冕之棄其城守，坦之疏於輔導，則君子所不取也。

translations.literal: Among the remaining men, Zhihan lost clean conduct, Gun lacked humane forbearance, Mian abandoned his city defense, and Tan was lax in guidance—what the noble man does not take.
translations.idiomatic: Among the remaining men, Zhihan lost clean conduct, Gun lacked humane forbearance, Mian abandoned his city defense, and Tan was lax in guidance—what the noble man does not take.
